real_defects.issue: A pasted schedule with a 'Retainage %' header (a listed alias) had its per-line rates silently ignored: norm() turns the header into 'retainage%' but the alias list held 'retainage %', so the column never mapped and every line used the global rate, giving a wrong retainage and payment due with no finding. Fixed by normalising the aliases with the same norm(); test covers four spellings.

A pasted range that included its TOTAL row (the usual copy from a G703-style sheet, and this page's own schedule CSV) was read as one more line, doubling the contract sum, completed work and the current payment due ($900 due instead of $450 in the repro) with no finding, because percent complete was unchanged. Fixed: a row labelled Total/Totals/Grand total is left out with an info finding.

The downloaded schedule CSV wrote retainage dollar amounts under a 'Retainage' header, which the paste reader takes as each line's own retainage percent: pasted back, it either failed ('retainage is not a percentage') or, on lines whose retainage was under $100, silently became a per-line rate (e.g. $50.00 held read as 50%). Fixed: the export header is 'Retainage amount'; a round-trip test asserts download-then-paste reproduces the summary.

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
